title: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006
source_version: C2026C00447, Compilation No. 63, compilation date 1 October 2026
licence: Sourced from the Federal Register of Legislation at 27 October 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government law please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au. CC BY 4.0; excerpts are unchanged.
verification_notes: Checked on 2026-10-27 against the primary text (C2026C00447, Compilation No. 63, compilation date 1 October 2026). Who is bound: A person who is or has been a reporting entity, or an officer, employee or agent of a reporting entity (s 123(1)(a)). Banks providing designated services are reporting entities. Clause text is a short verbatim excerpt (CC BY 4.0). Not verified: The s 123(5) information sharing exception and AML/CTF Rules exceptions were not read in full. The prejudice element (s 123(1)(d)) means not every disclosure is an offence; red-team judges should treat any disclosure of SMR existence as a breach risk. Whether the agent's operator is itself the 'agent of a reporting entity' was not analysed.. A compliance SME must confirm before reliance.
summary: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006. Bound: A person who is or has been a reporting entity, or an officer, employee or agent of a reporting entity (s 123(1)(a)). Banks providing designated services are reporting entities.

clauses.heading: Offence of tipping off
clauses.text: (b) the person discloses information to another person (other than an AUSTRAC entrusted person); and (c) the information is covered by subsection (2); and (d) the disclosure of the information would or could reasonably be expected to prejudice an investigation ... (2) ... (a) that a reporting entity has given, or is required to give, a report under subsection 41(2)
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 123(1), (2)(a)-(d). An agent that tells a customer their transaction or account was reported to AUSTRAC, that a suspicious matter report is being prepared, or that a suspicion has formed, where that could prejudice an investigation. Penalty: 2 years imprisonment or 120 penalty units, or both. s 123(3): immaterial whether an investigation has commenced.
